summary: Registers with IANA a new media feature tag for the message media type. The tag shows that a device supports message as a streaming media type, and such tags can be used to route calls to capable devices. This is an informational registration.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4569 adds a label for a device that supports message as streaming media. Other systems can use that information when choosing where to route a call.

questions: sip feature tag for instant messaging
what is the sip.message feature tag
what does the message media tag indicate
subtitle: An IANA media feature tag for devices that support message as streaming media.

tldr.problem: The message media type was added to SDP after RFC 3840 registered feature tags for the SDP media types then defined.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4569 registers the Boolean feature tag sip.message to indicate support for message as a streaming media type.
tldr.outcome: The tag can describe device capabilities and help route calls to devices that support session-based instant messaging.

today: RFC 4569 is Informational. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why the Tag Was Added
sections.content: Session Description Protocol (SDP) defines media types. RFC 3840 registered media feature tags for the types in the SDP specification that existed at the time, but that version did not define the message media type. A later revision of SDP added it, so this RFC registers a corresponding feature tag.
sections.plainLanguage: The message media type was added after an earlier set of capability labels was registered. This RFC supplies its missing label.

sections.title: The sip.message Feature Tag
sections.content: The registered media feature tag is sip.message, with ASN.1 identifier 21. Its value is Boolean. It indicates that a device supports message as a streaming media type, and is intended for describing device capabilities in communications applications.
sections.plainLanguage: The tag has a yes-or-no value. It tells others whether a device supports message as a streaming media type.

sections.title: Using the Capability
sections.content: The RFC gives routing a call to a phone that can support session-based instant messaging as an example of typical use. The feature tag lets an application describe that capability when it needs to choose a suitable device. The security considerations for the tag are those discussed in Section 11.1 of RFC 3840.
sections.plainLanguage: An application can use the tag to find a device that supports session-based instant messaging. The RFC points to RFC 3840 for related security considerations.
